newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wine makers mull govt legal action.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wine makers mull govt legal action.

text.p: The Australian Winemakers Federation is considering legal action against the federal government over its decision not to pay grants to 600 small winemakers from the 1995/96 financial year.

Federation chief executive Ian Sutton told Reuters on Thursday that winemakers would first seek a political solution to the issue but was seeking legal advice on a possible class action by the affected winemakers.

Sutton said cash grants of A$3.6 million, A$6,000 for each of the 600 winemakers, were due to offset an increase in wholesale sales tax on July 1, 1995 to 26 percent under a heads of agreement signed with the former Labor Government.
Sutton said the Howard Government's decision in this year's budget not to honour the payment was a serious policy precedent.
"We think the government has looked at the cash grants as forward expenditure, rather than as retrospective and that is where we think they have got some bad advice," he said.

Sutton said the federation was awaiting a response from its meeting last week with Primary Industries Minister John Anderson and if he failed to reverse the decision would take the issue to Treasurer Peter Costello and Prime Minister John Howard.
It would also ask the government to review the "insidious" tax on wine samples which was at the core of the issue, he said.

Sutton said winemakers accepted the cash grant would not have continued in 1996/97, but believing the government would honour the agreement they had already committed the 1995/96 payment into winery reinvestment.
"The small winemaker is doing it pretty tough at the moment," he said.
